name: Plectrum
author: creativecortexuk

sections.description:
Plectrum parses square-bracket chord notation inside song lyrics and renders the chord directly above the following lyric segment.

Features include:

  • Shortcode rendering for chord-marked content
  • Optional automatic processing for selected public post types
  • Browser-generated SVG ukulele chord diagrams for gCEA
  • Per-song transpose, size, diagram visibility, and print controls
  • Focused print output with optional footer notice
  • Multiple song instances per page without shared control state
  • Extensible hooks for rendering, aliases, settings, and lifecycle events

Example authoring format:

There [Am]once was a ship that put to sea

Shortcode usage:

[ukulele_chords]There [Am]once was a ship that put to sea[/ukulele_chords]

Supported shortcode attributes:

  • controls="true|false"
  • diagrams="true|false"
  • transpose="0"
  • print_button="true|false"
  • print_diagrams="true|false"
  • tuning="gCEA"
  • enharmonic_preference="auto|preserve-source|sharps|flats"

Literal square brackets can be escaped using doubled brackets such as [[Am]].
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin zip through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, or copy the plugin folder into /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate Plectrum through the WordPress plugins screen.
  3. Visit Settings > Plectrum to configure automatic processing, diagram defaults, print settings, and uninstall behavior.
  4. Add [ukulele_chords]...[/ukulele_chords] to song content, or enable automatic processing for your chosen post types.
sections.faq:
Does Plectrum change the stored post content?

No. Rendering and transposition happen at display time only.

What happens if a chord is unknown?

The chord name still renders above the lyric segment, but no diagram is shown.

Can I use Plectrum without automatic processing?

Yes. The shortcode is fully supported on its own.

Does it support multiple songs on the same page?

Yes. Each rendered song instance manages its own controls, transpose state, diagram visibility, and print targeting.

1.1

  • Sanitize filtered controls, chord names, and SVG diagrams immediately before output
  • Refresh diagrams and voicing metadata together with transposed chord labels
  • Use movable voicings when the transposed chord has no exact library entry
  • Use WordPress.org automatic translation loading

1.0

  • Add the Eb chord diagram with separate fingers and a D# alias
  • Add a settings-page guide to chord markup with a copyable Greensleeves example
  • Include the software disclaimer and DigitalArena plugin links

0.1.11

  • Update plugin and author links to the author plugins page
  • Display the software warranty and liability disclaimer on the settings page

0.1.10

  • Use the canonical plectrum plugin folder to match the translation domain
  • Add plugin license and bundled language directory headers; remove the hidden language placeholder
  • Register bundled translations on init and prefix the uninstall settings variable
  • Record successful site-owner testing on WordPress 7.1.3

0.1.9

  • Standardize JavaScript and documentation formatting and tidy variable declarations
  • Modernize screen-reader clipping and print break properties while preserving focused song printing

0.1.8

  • Prime front-end assets earlier in the request so plugin CSS and JavaScript load before rendered song markup appears

0.1.3

  • Fix initial front-end diagram rendering so browser-generated SVG diagrams receive their configuration before first paint

0.1.2

  • Ensure browser-rendered chord diagrams replace the server placeholder output after page load

0.1.1

  • Tightened the default chord diagram size for inline readability
  • Added visible string and fret labels to rendered chord diagrams

  • Chord parsing with escaped bracket support
